questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q49
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A flocculation tank contains 1800 m³ of water, which is mixed using paddles at an average velocity gradient G of 100/s. The water temperature and the corresponding dynamic viscosity are 30°C and 0.798×10⁻³ Ns/m², respectively. The theoretical power required to achieve the stated value of G (in kW, up to two decimal places) is ______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Volume of tank: \(V = 1800\text{ m}^3\)
    • Velocity gradient: \(G = 100\text{ s}^{-1}\)
    • Dynamic viscosity at 30°C: \(\mu = 0.798 \times 10^{-3}\text{ Ns/m}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the theoretical power (\(P\)) required in kW.

3. Core Concepts:

Camp and Stein's Equation for Flocculation: The temporal mean velocity gradient \(G\) in a mixing tank is given by:\[G = \sqrt{\dfrac{P}{\mu \cdot V}}\]where \(P\) is the power imparted to the water in Watts (W), \(\mu\) is dynamic viscosity, and \(V\) is the tank volume.

4. Solution Method:

Rearrange the velocity gradient equation to solve for \(P\). Obtain the result in Watts, then divide by 1000 to convert to kW.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Rearrange the formula:\[P = G^2 \cdot \mu \cdot V\]
  2. Substitute the values:\[P = (100)^2 \times (0.798 \times 10^{-3}) \times 1800\]\[P = 10000 \times 0.000798 \times 1800 = 7.98 \times 1800 = 14364\text{ W}\]
  3. Convert to kW:\[P = \dfrac{14364}{1000} = 14.364\text{ kW}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 14.36 kW | Accepted key range: 14.00 to 15.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A coal containing 2% sulfur is burned completely to ash in a brick kiln at a rate of 30 kg/min. The sulfur content in the ash was found to be 6% of the initial amount of sulfur present in the coal fed to the brick kiln. The molecular weights of S, H and O are 32, 1 and 16 g/mole, respectively. The annual rate of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) emission from the kiln (in tonnes/year, up to two decimal places) is ______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Coal burn rate = \(30\text{ kg/min}\)
    • Sulfur (S) content in coal = 2%
    • Sulfur retained in ash = 6% of the initial sulfur
    • Molecular weights: S = 32, O = 16 (therefore \(\text{SO}_2 = 32 + 2(16) = 64\))
  • Aim: Calculate the annual rate of sulfur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)) emission in tonnes/year.

3. Core Concepts:

Mass Balance: Total mass of sulfur input = Mass of sulfur in ash + Mass of sulfur emitted into the air.

Stoichiometry of Combustion: \(\text{S} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2\)
1 mole of Sulfur (32 kg) produces 1 mole of \(\text{SO}_2\) (64 kg). Therefore, the mass of \(\text{SO}_2\) produced is twice the mass of sulfur combusted.

Unit Conversions: \(1\text{ year} = 365 \times 24 \times 60 = 525600\text{ min}\); \(1\text{ tonne} = 1000\text{ kg}\).

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the mass flow rate of sulfur entering the kiln. Determine the fraction of sulfur that escapes as gas. Convert that mass of sulfur to the corresponding mass of \(\text{SO}_2\). Finally, scale from kg/min to tonnes/year.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Initial Sulfur Feed Rate:\[S_{\text{in}} = 30\text{ kg/min} \times 0.02 = 0.60\text{ kg/min}\]
  2. Sulfur Emitted as Gas:
    Since 6% stays in ash, \(100\% - 6\% = 94\%\) gets emitted.\[S_{\text{emitted}} = 0.60\text{ kg/min} \times 0.94 = 0.564\text{ kg/min}\]
  3. Calculate \(\text{SO}_2\) Emission Rate:
    Using the molar weight ratio \(\left(\dfrac{64}{32} = 2\right)\):\[\text{SO}_{2,\text{emitted}} = 0.564\text{ kg/min} \times 2 = 1.128\text{ kg/min}\]
  4. Convert to Tonnes per Year:\[\text{Annual Rate} = 1.128 \times 60 \times 24 \times 365 = 1.128 \times 525600\text{ kg/year}\]\[= 592876.8\text{ kg/year} = \dfrac{592876.8}{1000} = 592.88\text{ tonnes/year}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 592.88 tonnes/year | Accepted key range: 590.00 to 595.00

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: At a small water treatment plant which has 4 filters, the rates of filtration and backwashing are 200 m³/d/m² and 1000 m³/d/m², respectively. Backwashing is done for 15 min per day. The maturation, which occurs initially as the filter is put back into service after cleaning, takes 30 min. It is proposed to recover the water being wasted during backwashing and maturation. The percentage increase in the filtered water produced (up to two decimal places) would be ______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment (Filtration)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Number of filters = 4
    • Rate of filtration (\(R_f\)) = \(200\text{ m}^3/\text{d/m}^2\)
    • Rate of backwashing (\(R_b\)) = \(1000\text{ m}^3/\text{d/m}^2\)
    • Time for backwashing (\(t_b\)) = \(15\text{ min/day}\)
    • Time for maturation (\(t_m\)) = \(30\text{ min/day}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the percentage increase in net filtered water produced if the water wasted during backwashing and maturation is recovered.

3. Core Concepts:

Filtration Cycle: Over a 24-hour day, a filter is not continuously producing water — it has downtimes for backwashing and maturation.

Maturation: Water filtered during the initial 30 minutes after cleaning is of sub-standard quality and is directed to the drain (wasted).

Backwash Water: High-pressure water pumped upwards to clean the filter is taken from the plant's already filtered water (Clear Water Reservoir) and is thus an internal consumption of produced water.

Net Filtered Water: Gross Water Filtered − Water consumed in backwashing.

4. Solution Method:

Since all rates are given per square metre (m²) of filter area, all calculations are performed for a unit area (1 m²) over one day. The number of filters does not change the per-m² ratios.

  1. Determine the exact duration the filter actually produces useful water.
  2. Calculate gross filtered water (\(V_f\)) and water consumed in backwashing (\(V_b\)).
  3. Calculate net filtered water (\(V_{net} = V_f - V_b\)) and water wasted during maturation (\(V_m\)).
  4. Compute the percentage increase if total wasted water (\(V_w = V_b + V_m\)) is recovered.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Time Distribution in a 24-hour Cycle:
    • Backwash downtime = \(15\text{ min} = 0.25\text{ h}\)
    • Maturation downtime = \(30\text{ min} = 0.50\text{ h}\)
    • Effective filtration time: \(t_f = 24 - 0.25 - 0.50 = 23.25\text{ h} = \dfrac{23.25}{24}\text{ days} = 0.96875\text{ days}\)
  2. Volumes per 1 m² per day:
    • Gross useful filtered water:\[V_f = R_f \times t_f = 200 \times 0.96875 = 193.75\text{ m}^3\]
    • Water wasted during maturation:\[V_m = 200 \times \dfrac{30}{1440} = 200 \times 0.020833 = 4.1667\text{ m}^3\]
    • Water utilized for backwashing:\[V_b = 1000 \times \dfrac{15}{1440} = 1000 \times 0.0104167 = 10.4167\text{ m}^3\]
  3. Net and Wasted Water:\[V_{net} = V_f - V_b = 193.75 - 10.4167 = 183.333\text{ m}^3\]\[V_w = V_b + V_m = 10.4167 + 4.1667 = 14.5834\text{ m}^3\]
  4. Percentage Increase:\[\text{\% Increase} = \dfrac{V_w}{V_{net}} \times 100 = \dfrac{14.5834}{183.333} \times 100 = 7.9545\%\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 7.95% | Accepted key range: 7.75 to 7.95

questions.title: GATE CE 2018 Set 2 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A schematic flow diagram of a completely mixed biological reactor with provision for recycling of solids is shown in the figure.



S₀, S = readily biodegradable soluble BOD, mg/L
Q, Qᵣ, Qw = flow rates, m³/d
X₀, X, Xₑ, X = microorganism concentrations (mixed-liquor volatile suspended solids or MLVSS), mg/L

The mean cell residence time (in days, up to one decimal place) is ______
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Engineering (Activated Sludge Process)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Influent flow: \(Q = 15000\text{ m}^3/\text{d}\)
    • Hydraulic detention time: \(t = 2\text{ h}\)
    • MLSS in aeration tank: \(X = 3000\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Waste sludge flow: \(Q_w = 50\text{ m}^3/\text{d}\)
    • Concentration of waste sludge: \(X_u = 10000\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Effluent flow = \(14950\text{ m}^3/\text{d}\), Effluent SS (\(X_e\)) \(\approx 0\text{ mg/L}\)
  • Aim: Determine the mean cell residence time (\(\theta_c\)) in days.

3. Core Concepts:

Mean Cell Residence Time (MCRT or \(\theta_c\)): Also known as Sludge Retention Time (SRT), it is the average time a unit of biomass stays within the biological reactor system.\[\theta_c = \dfrac{\text{Total Mass of Biomass in System}}{\text{Mass of Biomass Leaving System per day}} = \dfrac{V \times X}{(Q_w \times X_u) + (Q - Q_w) \times X_e}\]

Standard Assumption: Biomass in the secondary clarifier is neglected unless its volume is explicitly provided.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the aeration tank volume (\(V = Q \times t\)).
  2. Compute total mass of microorganisms in the tank (\(M_{in} = V \times X\)).
  3. Compute mass of microorganisms leaving via waste sludge and effluent (\(M_{out}\)).
  4. Divide total mass in tank by mass leaving per day.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Aeration Tank Volume (\(V\)):\[V = Q \times t = 15000\text{ m}^3/\text{d} \times \dfrac{2}{24}\text{ d} = 1250\text{ m}^3\]
  2. Total Mass of Biomass (\(M_{in}\)):\[M_{in} = V \times X = 1250\text{ m}^3 \times 3000\text{ g/m}^3 = 3{,}750{,}000\text{ g} = 3750\text{ kg}\](Using: \(1\text{ mg/L} = 1\text{ g/m}^3\))
  3. Mass of Biomass Leaving (\(M_{out}\)):\[M_{out} = (Q_w \times X_u) + ((Q - Q_w) \times X_e)\]\[M_{out} = (50\text{ m}^3/\text{d} \times 10000\text{ g/m}^3) + (14950\text{ m}^3/\text{d} \times 0) = 500{,}000\text{ g/d} = 500\text{ kg/d}\]
  4. MCRT (\(\theta_c\)):\[\theta_c = \dfrac{M_{in}}{M_{out}} = \dfrac{3750\text{ kg}}{500\text{ kg/d}} = 7.5\text{ days}\]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 7.5 days | Accepted key range: 7.5 to 7.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q13
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The reaction rate involving reactants \(A\) and \(B\) is given by \(-k[A]^\alpha[B]^\beta\). Which one of the following statements is valid for the reaction to be a first-order reaction?
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water & Wastewater Treatment Kinetics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Rate law \(r = -k[A]^\alpha[B]^\beta\)
  • Aim: Identify the condition for the reaction to be first-order.

3. Core Concepts:

The overall order of a reaction is the sum of powers of the concentration terms:

\[n = \alpha + \beta \]

For a first-order reaction: \(n = 1 \implies \alpha + \beta = 1\).

4. Solution Method:

Option\(\alpha\)\(\beta\)\(n = \alpha+\beta\)Order
A000Zero
B101First ✓
C112Second
D123Third

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\alpha = 1\) and \(\beta = 0\)  |  Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q14
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The wastewater from a city, containing a high concentration of biodegradable organics, is being steadily discharged into a flowing river at a location S. If the rate of aeration of the river water is lower than the rate of degradation of the organics, then the dissolved oxygen of the river water
options: is lowest at the location S.
is lowest at a point upstream of the location S.
remains constant all along the length of the river.
is lowest at a point downstream of the location S.

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: is lowest at the location S.
structuredOptions.html: is lowest at the location S.

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: is lowest at a point upstream of the location S.
structuredOptions.html: is lowest at a point upstream of the location S.

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: remains constant all along the length of the river.
structuredOptions.html: remains constant all along the length of the river.

structuredOptions.label: D
structuredOptions.text: is lowest at a point downstream of the location S.
structuredOptions.html: is lowest at a point downstream of the location S.

questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Disposal (River Kinetics)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data: Wastewater discharged at location S; high biodegradable organics; rate of aeration < rate of degradation (initially).
  • Aim: Determine the spatial location where dissolved oxygen (DO) is lowest.

3. Core Concepts:

The Streeter-Phelps DO Sag Curve describes two competing processes downstream of a discharge:

  • Deoxygenation: Bacteria consume DO to degrade organics (high initially due to high BOD).
  • Reaeration: Oxygen diffuses from the atmosphere (increases as DO deficit grows).

The DO minimum (critical deficit) occurs where the decreasing deoxygenation rate exactly equals the increasing reaeration rate — always at some distance downstream of the discharge point S.

4. Solution Method:

  • At S: DO drops due to dilution but is not yet at its lowest (biochemical consumption takes time).
  • Upstream of S: generally unpolluted (high DO).
  • Since initial degradation rate > reaeration rate, DO continues to fall downstream until the critical point is reached.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: DO is lowest at a point downstream of location S  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q15
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT present in the acid rain?
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Four compounds — \(\text{HNO}_3\), \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), \(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\)
  • Aim: Identify which compound is NOT typically a component of acid rain.

3. Core Concepts:

  • \(\text{HNO}_3\) (Nitric Acid): Key acid rain component — formed from \(\text{NO}_x\) emissions reacting with atmospheric moisture.
  • \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) (Sulfuric Acid): Key acid rain component — formed from \(\text{SO}_2\) emissions.
  • \(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\) (Carbonic Acid): Naturally present in all unpolluted rain (atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) dissolves in water); makes rain slightly acidic (pH ~5.6).
  • \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\) (Acetic Acid): Organic acid — NOT a constituent of standard acid rain driven by anthropogenic pollution.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\)  |  Correct option: (D)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The equivalent sound power level (in dB) of the four sources with the noise levels of 60 dB, 69 dB, 70 dB and 79 dB is _______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Noise Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Noise levels of four independent sources: \(L_1 = 60\text{ dB}\), \(L_2 = 69\text{ dB}\), \(L_3 = 70\text{ dB}\), \(L_4 = 79\text{ dB}\).
  • Aim: Determine the equivalent total sound level (\(L_{eq}\)) when all sources operate simultaneously.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Logarithmic Addition: Sound levels in dB cannot be added algebraically. The intensity ratio is: \(I/I_0 = 10^{L/10}\)
  • Equivalent Sound Level:
    \[L_{eq} = 10\log_{10}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} 10^{L_i/10}\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert each dB value to its acoustic intensity ratio \(10^{L/10}\).
  2. Sum the linear ratios.
  3. Convert back to dB using \(10\log_{10}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Intensity ratios and summation:
    \[\sum 10^{L_i/10} = 10^{6} + 10^{6.9} + 10^{7} + 10^{7.9} \]\[= 1{,}000{,}000 + 7{,}943{,}282 + 10{,}000{,}000 + 79{,}432{,}824 \]\[= 98{,}376{,}106 \]
  2. Convert back to dB:
    \[L_{eq} = 10\log_{10}(98{,}376{,}106) = 10 \times 7.9929 \approx 79.9\text{ dB} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 79.9 dB  |  Accepted key range: 79 to 81

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
The spherical grit particles, having a radius of 0.01 mm and specific gravity of 3.0, need to be separated in a settling chamber. It is given that
• g = 9.81 m/s²
• the density of the liquid in the settling chamber = 1000 kg/m³
• the kinematic viscosity of the liquid in the settling chamber = 10⁻⁶ m²/s
Assuming laminar conditions, the settling velocity (in mm/s, up to one decimal place) is _______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment (Sedimentation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Particle radius: \(r = 0.01 ext{ mm}\)
    • Specific gravity of grit: \(G_s = 3.0\)
    • \(g = 9.81 ext{ m/s}^2\), \( ho_l = 1000 ext{ kg/m}^3\)
    • Kinematic viscosity: \( u = 10^{-6} ext{ m}^2/ ext{s}\)
    • Flow regime: Laminar
  • Aim: Calculate the terminal settling velocity (\(V_s\)) in mm/s.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Stokes' Law (laminar settling, \(Re < 1\)):
    \[V_s = \dfrac{g\,(G_s - 1)\,d^2}{18\, u} \]where \(d\) is the particle diameter and \( u\) is the kinematic viscosity.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Extract diameter from given radius; convert to SI (meters).
  2. Substitute into Stokes' Law to get velocity in m/s.
  3. Convert to mm/s.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Unit preparation:
    \[d = 2 imes 0.01 ext{ mm} = 0.02 ext{ mm} = 2 imes 10^{-5} ext{ m} \]\[G_s - 1 = 2.0 \]
  2. Apply Stokes' Law:
    \[V_s = \dfrac{9.81 imes 2.0 imes (2 imes 10^{-5})^2}{18 imes 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{19.62 imes 4 imes 10^{-10}}{18 imes 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{78.48 imes 10^{-10}}{18 imes 10^{-6}} = 4.36 imes 10^{-4} ext{ m/s} \]
  3. Convert to mm/s:
    \[V_s = 4.36 imes 10^{-4} imes 1000 = 0.436 ext{ mm/s} \approx 0.4 ext{ mm/s} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.4 mm/s  |  Accepted key range: 0.3 to 0.5

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q54
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
Two wastewater streams A and B, having an identical ultimate BOD are getting mixed to form the stream C. The temperature of the stream A is 20°C and the temperature of the stream C is 10°C. It is given that
• the 5-day BOD of the stream A measured at 20°C = 50 mg/l
• BOD rate constant (base 10) at 20°C = 0.115 per day
• temperature coefficient = 1.135
The 5-day BOD (in mg/l, up to one decimal place) of the stream C, calculated at 10°C, is _______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Characteristics (BOD)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Streams A and B have identical ultimate BOD (\(L_0\))
    • Stream A: \(T_A = 20^\circ\text{C}\), \(y_{5,20} = 50\text{ mg/l}\)
    • Base-10 BOD rate constant at 20°C: \(K_{D,20} = 0.115\text{ day}^{-1}\)
    • Temperature coefficient: \(\theta = 1.135\)
    • Stream C (mixture): \(T_C = 10^\circ\text{C}\)
  • Aim: Determine the 5-day BOD of Stream C at 10°C (\(y_{5,10}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Ultimate BOD Invariance: Since streams A and B have the same \(L_0\), any mixture (Stream C) retains the same \(L_{0C} = L_0\).
  • BOD Kinetics (Base-10):
    \[y_t = L_0\left(1 - 10^{-K_D \cdot t}\right) \]
  • Temperature Correction:
    \[K_{D,T} = K_{D,20} \cdot \theta^{(T-20)} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Use 20°C data from Stream A to find \(L_0\).
  2. Adjust \(K_D\) to 10°C using the temperature coefficient \(\theta\).
  3. Calculate 5-day BOD of Stream C at 10°C.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Determine ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)):
    \[50 = L_0\left(1 - 10^{-0.115 \times 5}\right) = L_0\left(1 - 10^{-0.575}\right) \]\[50 = L_0(1 - 0.26607) = L_0 \times 0.73393 \]\[L_0 = \dfrac{50}{0.73393} = 68.13\text{ mg/l} \]
  2. Temperature correction for \(K_D\):
    \[K_{D,10} = 0.115 \times (1.135)^{(10-20)} = 0.115 \times (1.135)^{-10} = 0.115 \times 0.28179 = 0.03241\text{ day}^{-1} \]
  3. 5-day BOD at 10°C:
    \[y_{5,10} = 68.13 \times \left(1 - 10^{-0.03241 \times 5}\right) = 68.13 \times \left(1 - 10^{-0.16205}\right) \]\[= 68.13 \times (1 - 0.68857) = 68.13 \times 0.31143 \approx 21.2\text{ mg/l} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 21.2 mg/l  |  Accepted key range: 20.0 to 22.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 1 | CE Q55
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The wastewater having an organic concentration of 54 mg/l is flowing at a steady rate of 0.8 m³/day through a detention tank of dimensions 2 m × 4 m × 2 m. If the contents of the tank are well mixed and the decay constant is 0.1 per day, the outlet concentration (in mg/l, up to one decimal place) is _______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Reactor Kinetics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Inlet concentration: \(C_{in} = 54\text{ mg/l}\)
    • Flow rate: \(Q = 0.8\text{ m}^3/\text{day}\)
    • Tank dimensions: \(2\text{ m} \times 4\text{ m} \times 2\text{ m}\) (well-mixed)
    • First-order decay constant: \(k = 0.1\text{ day}^{-1}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the steady-state outlet concentration (\(C_{out}\)).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Reactor Type: "Well-mixed" implies a Completely Mixed Flow Reactor (CMFR / CSTR).
  • Hydraulic Retention Time: \(\theta = V/Q\)
  • Steady-State Mass Balance (first-order decay, accumulation \(= 0\)):
    \[Q\,C_{in} - Q\,C_{out} - V k\,C_{out} = 0 \implies C_{out} = \dfrac{C_{in}}{1 + k\theta} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate tank volume \(V\).
  2. Determine HRT \(\theta = V/Q\).
  3. Apply the CMFR steady-state equation to find \(C_{out}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Tank volume and HRT:
    \[V = 2 \times 4 \times 2 = 16\text{ m}^3 \]\[\theta = \dfrac{16}{0.8} = 20\text{ days} \]
  2. Effluent concentration:
    \[C_{out} = \dfrac{54}{1 + (0.1 \times 20)} = \dfrac{54}{1 + 2} = \dfrac{54}{3} = 18.0\text{ mg/l} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 18.0 mg/l  |  Accepted key range: 17.9 to 18.1

questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
Following observations have been made for the elevation and temperature to ascertain the stability of the atmosphere:
Elevation (in m)Temperature (in °C)
1015.5
6015.0
13014.3

The atmosphere is classified as
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Elevation \(z_1 = 10 \text{ m}\), Temperature \(T_1 = 15.5^\circ\text{C}\)
    • Elevation \(z_2 = 60 \text{ m}\), Temperature \(T_2 = 15.0^\circ\text{C}\)
    • Elevation \(z_3 = 130 \text{ m}\), Temperature \(T_3 = 14.3^\circ\text{C}\)
  • Aim: Classify the atmospheric stability based on the observed temperature profile.

3. Core Concepts:

Environmental Lapse Rate (ELR): The actual observed rate of decrease of temperature with altitude:\[ELR = -\dfrac{\Delta T}{\Delta z} \]

Dry Adiabatic Lapse Rate (DALR): The theoretical rate at which a dry air parcel cools as it rises \(\approx 9.8^\circ\text{C/km}\).

Stability Criteria:

  • \(ELR > DALR\): Super-adiabatic → Unstable
  • \(ELR < DALR\): Sub-adiabatic → Stable
  • \(ELR = DALR\): Neutral

4. Solution Method:

Calculate the actual ELR from field observations and compare with the standard DALR.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. ELR for layer 1 (10 m to 60 m):
    \(\Delta z = 50 \text{ m} = 0.05 \text{ km}\),   \(\Delta T = 15.0 - 15.5 = -0.5^\circ\text{C}\)\[ELR_1 = -\dfrac{-0.5}{0.05} = 10^\circ\text{C/km} \]
  2. ELR for layer 2 (60 m to 130 m):
    \(\Delta z = 70 \text{ m} = 0.07 \text{ km}\),   \(\Delta T = 14.3 - 15.0 = -0.7^\circ\text{C}\)\[ELR_2 = -\dfrac{-0.7}{0.07} = 10^\circ\text{C/km} \]
  3. Compare ELR with DALR:
    Uniform \(ELR = 10^\circ\text{C/km} > 9.8^\circ\text{C/km}\) (DALR)
    Since \(ELR > DALR\), the atmosphere is highly convective and unstable.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: Unstable | Correct option: (B)

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
The composition of a municipal solid waste sample is given below:
ComponentPercent by MassMoisture Content (%)Energy Content (kJ/kg, on as-discarded basis)
Food Waste20702500
Paper10410000
Cardboard1048000
Plastics10114000
Garden Trimmings40603500
Wood52014000
Tin Cans52100

The difference between the energy content of the waste sample calculated on dry basis and as-discarded basis (in kJ/kg) would be ___________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Solid Waste Management

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data: Table of MSW composition — Mass (%), Moisture (%), and As-discarded Energy Content (kJ/kg).
  • Aim: Find the difference between energy content on a dry basis and an as-discarded (wet) basis in kJ/kg.

3. Core Concepts:

As-Discarded Energy (\(E_{wet}\)): Energy per kg of raw wet waste sample.

Dry Basis Energy (\(E_{dry}\)): Since moisture contributes no energy but adds weight, removing water increases specific energy per unit mass:\[E_{dry} = \dfrac{\text{Total Energy}}{\text{Total Dry Mass}} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Assume a basis of 100 kg of as-discarded MSW.
  2. Determine the total energy of the 100 kg sample.
  3. Compute total dry mass by subtracting the moisture mass of each component.
  4. Evaluate \(E_{wet}\) and \(E_{dry}\), then compute the difference.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Basis: 100 kg of MSW

ComponentMass (kg)Moisture (kg)Dry Mass (kg)Energy (kJ)
Food Waste20\(20 \times 0.70 = 14\)6\(20 \times 2500 = 50{,}000\)
Paper10\(10 \times 0.04 = 0.4\)9.6\(10 \times 10000 = 100{,}000\)
Cardboard10\(10 \times 0.04 = 0.4\)9.6\(10 \times 8000 = 80{,}000\)
Plastics10\(10 \times 0.01 = 0.1\)9.9\(10 \times 14000 = 140{,}000\)
Garden Trimmings40\(40 \times 0.60 = 24\)16\(40 \times 3500 = 140{,}000\)
Wood5\(5 \times 0.20 = 1\)4\(5 \times 14000 = 70{,}000\)
Tin Cans5\(5 \times 0.02 = 0.1\)4.9\(5 \times 100 = 500\)
Total100—60580,500

Energy Content Calculations:

\[E_{wet} = \dfrac{580{,}500 \text{ kJ}}{100 \text{ kg}} = 5805 \text{ kJ/kg} \]\[E_{dry} = \dfrac{580{,}500 \text{ kJ}}{60 \text{ kg}} = 9675 \text{ kJ/kg} \]\[\text{Difference} = 9675 - 5805 = 3870 \text{ kJ/kg} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 3870 kJ/kg | Accepted key range: 3850 to 3900

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: For a given water sample, the ratio between BOD₅-day, 20°C and the ultimate BOD is 0.68. The value of the reaction rate constant k (on base e) (in day⁻¹, up to two decimal places) is ___________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Waste Water Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Time: \(t = 5 \text{ days}\)
    • Ratio of \(\text{BOD}_5\) to Ultimate BOD: \(\dfrac{y_5}{L_0} = 0.68\)
  • Aim: Calculate the deoxygenation reaction rate constant \(k\) (base \(e\)) in day\(^{-1}\), to two decimal places.

3. Core Concepts:

First Order BOD Kinetics:\[\text{BOD}_t = L_0 \left(1 - e^{-kt}\right) \]where \(\text{BOD}_t\) is oxygen consumed at time \(t\), \(L_0\) is the ultimate carbonaceous BOD, and \(k\) is the rate constant (base \(e\)).

4. Solution Method:

  1. Substitute the given ratio into the first-order kinetic equation.
  2. Isolate the exponential term and use the natural logarithm (\(\ln\)) to solve for \(k\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

\[\dfrac{\text{BOD}_5}{L_0} = 1 - e^{-5k} \]\[0.68 = 1 - e^{-5k} \]\[e^{-5k} = 1 - 0.68 = 0.32 \]Taking natural logarithm on both sides:\[-5k = \ln(0.32) = -1.1394 \]\[k = \dfrac{1.1394}{5} = 0.2279 \approx 0.23 \text{ day}^{-1} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.23 day\(^{-1}\) | Accepted key range: 0.22 to 0.24

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A municipal corporation is required to treat 1000 m³/day of water. It is found that an overflow rate of 20 m/day will produce a satisfactory removal of the discrete suspended particles at a depth of 3 m. The diameter (in meters, rounded to the nearest integer) of a circular settling tank designed for the removal of these particles would be ___________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Flow rate: \(Q = 1000 \text{ m}^3/\text{day}\)
    • Surface Overflow Rate: \(V_0 = 20 \text{ m/day}\)
    • Depth of tank: \(H = 3 \text{ m}\) (distractor — not required for diameter)
    • Tank Shape: Circular
  • Aim: Find the diameter of the settling tank in meters, rounded to the nearest integer.

3. Core Concepts:

Surface Overflow Rate (SOR): Represents the settling velocity of the slowest particle that will be 100% removed. Defined by plan area:\[V_0 = \dfrac{Q}{A_s} \]

Plan Area of Circular Tank: \(A_s = \dfrac{\pi D^2}{4}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Calculate the required surface area (\(A_s\)) from flow rate and overflow rate.
  2. Calculate the corresponding diameter for a circular tank.
  3. Round to the nearest integer.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Required Surface Area:\[A_s = \dfrac{Q}{V_0} = \dfrac{1000}{20} = 50 \text{ m}^2 \]
  2. Calculate Diameter:\[\dfrac{\pi D^2}{4} = 50 \implies D^2 = \dfrac{200}{\pi} = 63.662 \text{ m}^2 \implies D = \sqrt{63.662} = 7.978 \text{ m} \]
  3. Rounding: \(D \approx 8 \text{ m}\)

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8 m | Accepted key range: 8 to 8

questions.title: GATE CE 2017 Set 2 | CE Q53
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
The analysis of a water sample produces the following results:
Ionmilligram per milli-equivalent for the ionConcentration (mg/L)
Ca²⁺20.060
Mg²⁺12.236.6
Na⁺23.092
K⁺39.178.2
Cl⁻35.571
SO₄²⁻48.072
HCO₃⁻61.0122

The total hardness (in mg/L as CaCO₃) of the water sample is ___________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Quality

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    IonConcentration (mg/L)Equivalent Weight (mg/meq)
    \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\)6020.0
    \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\)36.612.2
    \(\text{Na}^+\), \(\text{K}^+\), \(\text{Cl}^-\), \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\), \(\text{HCO}_3^-\)Listed (not hardness contributors)
  • Aim: Calculate Total Hardness in mg/L as \(\text{CaCO}_3\).

3. Core Concepts:

Total Hardness (TH): Caused by multivalent cations — predominantly \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) and \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\). Monovalent ions (\(\text{Na}^+\), \(\text{K}^+\)) do not contribute to hardness.

\[ \text{TH (as CaCO}_3) = \left( \dfrac{[\text{Ca}^{2+}]}{\text{Eq.Wt of Ca}} + \dfrac{[\text{Mg}^{2+}]}{\text{Eq.Wt of Mg}} \right) \times \text{Eq.Wt of CaCO}_3 \]

Equivalent Weight of \(\text{CaCO}_3\): \(\dfrac{100}{2} = 50 \text{ mg/meq}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Identify multivalent cations causing hardness (\(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) and \(\text{Mg}^{2+}\)).
  2. Calculate their concentrations in meq/L.
  3. Sum the equivalents and multiply by the equivalent weight of \(\text{CaCO}_3\) (50 mg/meq).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert concentrations to meq/L:\[\text{Ca}^{2+} = \dfrac{60}{20.0} = 3.0 \text{ meq/L} \]\[\text{Mg}^{2+} = \dfrac{36.6}{12.2} = 3.0 \text{ meq/L} \]
  2. Total Hardness as \(\text{CaCO}_3\):\[\text{Total} = 3.0 + 3.0 = 6.0 \text{ meq/L} \]\[\text{TH as CaCO}_3 = 6.0 \times 50 = 300 \text{ mg/L} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 300 mg/L | Accepted key range: 300 to 300

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q18
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: Crown corrosion in a reinforced concrete sewer is caused by:
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Engineering — Crown Corrosion in Sewers

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Concrete sewer system.
  • Aim: Identify the gas responsible for crown corrosion.

3. Core Concepts:

Crown Corrosion Mechanism:

  1. Under anaerobic conditions, sulfate-reducing bacteria convert sulfates to Hydrogen Sulfide (\(H_2S\)) gas.
  2. \(H_2S\) rises to the crown (top) of the sewer where moisture and oxygen are present.
  3. Aerobic bacteria (Thiobacillus) oxidize \(H_2S\) to Sulfuric Acid (\(H_2SO_4\)).
  4. \(H_2SO_4\) corrodes the concrete crown.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

\(\text{CO}_2\), \(\text{CH}_4\), and \(\text{NH}_3\) do not undergo biological conversion to strong mineral acids in sewers. \(H_2S\) is the essential intermediate.

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(H_2S\) | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: It was decided to construct a fabric filter, using bags of 0.45 m diameter and 7.5 m long, for removing industrial stack gas containing particulates. The expected rate of airflow into the filter is 10 m3/s. If the filtering velocity is 2.0 m/min, the minimum number of bags (rounded to nearest higher integer) required for continuous cleaning operation is
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution Control — Baghouse Filter

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Bag diameter: \(D = 0.45\text{ m}\)
    • Bag length: \(L = 7.5\text{ m}\)
    • Airflow rate: \(Q = 10\text{ m}^3/\text{s}\)
    • Filtering velocity: \(v = 2.0\text{ m/min}\)
  • Aim: Find the minimum number of filter bags required for continuous operation.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total filtration area required: \(A_{\text{total}} = Q/v\)
  • Lateral surface area of one cylindrical bag: \(A_{\text{bag}} = \pi \times D \times L\)
  • Number of bags: \(N = A_{\text{total}} / A_{\text{bag}}\) (round up to next integer)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert \(Q\) to m³/min:\[Q = 10 \times 60 = 600\text{ m}^3/\text{min} \]
  2. Total area required:\[A_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{600}{2.0} = 300\text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Area of one bag:\[A_{\text{bag}} = \pi \times 0.45 \times 7.5 \approx 10.603\text{ m}^2 \]
  4. Number of bags:\[N = \dfrac{300}{10.603} \approx 28.29 \implies \text{round up to } \mathbf{29} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 29 bags | Correct option: (B)

questions.question: Effluent from an industry 'A' has a pH of 4.2. The effluent from another industry 'B' has double the hydroxyl (OH-) ion concentration than the effluent from industry 'A'. pH of effluent from the industry 'B' will be _______________
questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • \(\text{pH}_A = 4.2\)
    • \([\text{OH}^-]_B = 2 \times [\text{OH}^-]_A\)
  • Aim: Find the pH of industry B.

3. Core Concepts:

  • \(\text{pH} + \text{pOH} = 14\) (at standard conditions)
  • \(\text{pOH} = -\log_{10}[\text{OH}^-]\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Find \([\text{OH}^-]\) of effluent A:\[\text{pOH}_A = 14 - \text{pH}_A = 14 - 4.2 = 9.8 \]\[ [\text{OH}^-]_A = 10^{-9.8}\text{ mol/L} \]
  2. Determine \([\text{OH}^-]\) and pOH for effluent B:\[ [\text{OH}^-]_B = 2 \times 10^{-9.8}\text{ mol/L} \]\[\text{pOH}_B = -\log_{10}(2 \times 10^{-9.8}) = 9.8 - \log_{10}(2) = 9.8 - 0.301 = 9.499 \]
  3. Calculate pH of effluent B:\[\text{pH}_B = 14 - \text{pOH}_B = 14 - 9.499 = 4.501 \]

5. Final Answer:

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: An electrostatic precipitator (ESP) with 5600 m2 of collector plate area is 96 percent efficient in treating 185 m3/s of flue gas from a 200 MW thermal power plant. It was found that in order to achieve 97 percent efficiency, the collector plate area should be 6100 m2. In order to increase the efficiency to 99 percent, the ESP collector plate area (expressed in m2) would be _______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution — Electrostatic Precipitator (ESP)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(A_1 = 5600\text{ m}^2\), \(\eta_1 = 0.96\)
    • \(A_2 = 6100\text{ m}^2\), \(\eta_2 = 0.97\)
    • Target efficiency: \(\eta_3 = 0.99\)
  • Aim: Find the collector plate area \(A_3\) required for 99% efficiency.

3. Core Concepts:

Deutsch-Anderson Equation:\[\eta = 1 - e^{-\dfrac{wA}{Q}} \implies \ln(1-\eta) = -\dfrac{wA}{Q} \]Assuming constant drift velocity \(w\) and flow rate \(Q\), the plate area \(A\) is directly proportional to \(-\ln(1-\eta)\).

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Proportional Relationship:\[\dfrac{A_3}{A_1} = \dfrac{\ln(1-\eta_3)}{\ln(1-\eta_1)} \]
  2. Substitute and Solve (using 96% pair):\[A_3 = 5600 \times \dfrac{\ln(0.01)}{\ln(0.04)} = 5600 \times \dfrac{-4.60517}{-3.21888} = 5600 \times 1.43068 \approx 8011.8\text{ m}^2 \]Verification using 97% pair: \(A_3 = 6100 \times \dfrac{\ln(0.01)}{\ln(0.03)} \approx 8011.1\text{ m}^2\) ✓

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 8012 m² | Accepted key range: [8000, 8040]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 1 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The 2-day and 4-day BOD values of a sewage sample are 100 mg/L and 155 mg/L, respectively. The value of BOD rate constant (expressed in per day) is _______________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Engineering — BOD Rate Constant

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • \(BOD_2 = 100\text{ mg/L}\)
    • \(BOD_4 = 155\text{ mg/L}\)
  • Aim: Find the BOD rate constant \(k\) (base \(e\)) in day⁻¹.

3. Core Concepts:

First-order BOD exertion equation:\[Y_t = L_0(1 - e^{-kt}) \]where \(Y_t\) = BOD exerted at time \(t\), \(L_0\) = ultimate BOD, \(k\) = rate constant.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Set up simultaneous equations:\[L_0(1 - e^{-2k}) = 100 \quad \cdots (1) \]\[L_0(1 - e^{-4k}) = 155 \quad \cdots (2) \]
  2. Solve the ratio to eliminate \(L_0\):
    Let \(x = e^{-2k}\), so \(e^{-4k} = x^2\).\[\dfrac{Y_4}{Y_2} = \dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 - x} = \dfrac{(1-x)(1+x)}{(1-x)} = 1 + x \]\[1 + x = \dfrac{155}{100} = 1.55 \implies x = 0.55 \]
  3. Solve for \(k\):\[e^{-2k} = 0.55 \implies -2k = \ln(0.55) = -0.5978 \]\[k = \dfrac{0.5978}{2} = 0.2989\text{ day}^{-1} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.30 day⁻¹ | Accepted key range: [0.29, 0.31]

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q18

questions.question: A water supply board is responsible for treating 1500 m³/day of water. A settling column analysis indicates that an overflow rate of 20 m/day will produce satisfactory removal for a depth of 3.1 m. It is decided to have two circular settling tanks in parallel. The required diameter (expressed in m) of the settling tanks is _________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Total discharge \(Q = 1500\text{ m}^3/\text{day}\)
    • Overflow rate (Surface loading rate) \(V_0 = 20\text{ m/day}\)
    • Number of parallel tanks \(n = 2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the required diameter (\(D\)) of one circular settling tank.

3. Core Concepts:

In ideal sedimentation, particle removal depends exclusively on the surface overflow rate (\(V_0\)) and surface area (\(A\)):

\[V_0 = \dfrac{Q_{\text{total}}}{A_{\text{total}}} \]

4. Solution Method & Execution:

  1. Total required surface area:\[A_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{1500}{20} = 75\text{ m}^2 \]
  2. Surface area per tank:\[A_{\text{each}} = \dfrac{75}{2} = 37.5\text{ m}^2 \]
  3. Calculate diameter (\(D\)):\[\dfrac{\pi}{4}D^2 = 37.5 \implies D^2 = \dfrac{150}{\pi} \approx 47.746\text{ m}^2 \]\[D = \sqrt{47.746} \approx 6.91\text{ m} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 6.91 m | Accepted key range: 6.8 to 7.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q19
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The hardness of a ground water sample was found to be 420 mg/L as CaCO₃. A softener containing ion exchange resins was installed to reduce the total hardness to 75 mg/L as CaCO₃ before supplying to 4 households. Each household gets treated water at a rate of 540 L/day. If the efficiency of the softener is 100%, the bypass flow rate (expressed in L/day) is _________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Softening

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Initial raw water hardness: \(H_i = 420\text{ mg/L as CaCO}_3\)
    • Target supplied hardness: \(H_f = 75\text{ mg/L as CaCO}_3\)
    • Number of households = 4, water supply = 540 L/day per household
    • Softener efficiency = 100% → effluent hardness \(H_s = 0\text{ mg/L}\)
  • Aim: Calculate the bypass flow rate (\(Q_{\text{bypass}}\)) in L/day.

3. Core Concepts:

A portion of raw water is bypassed around the softener and blended with fully softened water to achieve the target hardness. Mass Balance Equation:

\[Q_{\text{bypass}} \cdot H_i + Q_{\text{softener}} \cdot H_s = Q_{\text{total}} \cdot H_f \]

4. Solution Method & Execution:

  1. Total Daily Demand (\(Q_{\text{total}}\)):\[Q_{\text{total}} = 4 \times 540 = 2160\text{ L/day} \]
  2. Mass Balance:\[Q_{\text{bypass}} \times 420 + 0 = 2160 \times 75 = 162{,}000 \]
  3. Solve for \(Q_{\text{bypass}}\):\[Q_{\text{bypass}} = \dfrac{162{,}000}{420} = 385.71\text{ L/day} \]

5. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 385.71 L/day | Accepted key range: 380 to 390

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q20
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: The sound pressure (expressed in μPa) of the faintest sound that a normal healthy individual can hear is
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Noise Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Aim: Determine the reference sound pressure of the faintest sound audible to a normal healthy human.

3. Core Concepts:

The Sound Pressure Level (SPL) in decibels is given by:

\[\text{SPL (dB)} = 20\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{P}{P_0}\right) \]

The absolute threshold of human hearing at 1000 Hz represents 0 dB. Setting SPL = 0:

\[0 = 20\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{P}{P_0}\right) \implies P = P_0 \]

The universally accepted standard reference sound pressure in air is \(P_0 = 20\,\mu\text{Pa}\) (i.e., \(2 \times 10^{-5}\text{ Pa}\)).

4. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 20 μPa | Correct option: (C)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q50
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
A sample of water has been analyzed for common ions and results are presented in the form of a bar diagram as shown.



The non-carbonate hardness (expressed in mg/L as CaCO₃) of the sample is
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Quality

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data (from bar diagram in meq/L):
    • \(Ca^{2+}\) ends at 2.65 → \(Ca^{2+} = 2.65\text{ meq/L}\)
    • \(Mg^{2+}\) spans from 2.65 to 4.10 → \(Mg^{2+} = 1.45\text{ meq/L}\)
    • \(HCO_3^-\) spans from 0 to 3.30 → \(HCO_3^- = 3.30\text{ meq/L}\)
  • Aim: Evaluate Non-Carbonate Hardness (NCH) in mg/L as \(\text{CaCO}_3\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total Hardness (TH): Sum of \(Ca^{2+}\) and \(Mg^{2+}\) concentrations (meq/L).
  • Alkalinity: Represented by \(HCO_3^-\), \(CO_3^{2-}\), and \(OH^-\) ions.
  • Carbonate Hardness (CH):
    • If Alk < TH → CH = Alk
    • If Alk ≥ TH → CH = TH
  • Non-Carbonate Hardness: \(NCH = TH - CH\)
  • Unit Conversion: \(\text{mg/L as CaCO}_3 = \text{meq/L} \times 50\text{ mg/meq}\)

4. Solution Method:

  1. Extract ion concentrations from the bar diagram.
  2. Calculate Total Hardness (TH) and Alkalinity.
  3. Compare TH and Alkalinity to find Carbonate Hardness (CH).
  4. Subtract CH from TH to get NCH in meq/L.
  5. Multiply by 50 to convert to mg/L as \(\text{CaCO}_3\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Total Hardness and Alkalinity:\[TH = 2.65 + 1.45 = 4.10\text{ meq/L} \]\[\text{Alkalinity} = HCO_3^- = 3.30\text{ meq/L} \]
  2. Carbonate and Non-Carbonate Hardness:
    Since Alkalinity (3.30) < TH (4.10):\[CH = 3.30\text{ meq/L} \]\[NCH = 4.10 - 3.30 = 0.80\text{ meq/L} \]
  3. Convert to mg/L as \(\text{CaCO}_3\):\[NCH = 0.80 \times 50 = 40\text{ mg/L} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 40 mg/L | Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q51
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A noise meter located at a distance of 30 m from a point source recorded 74 dB. The reading at a distance of 60 m from the point source would be _________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Noise Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Noise level \(L_1 = 74\text{ dB}\) at distance \(r_1 = 30\text{ m}\)
    • Target distance \(r_2 = 60\text{ m}\)
  • Aim: Determine the noise reading (\(L_2\)) at 60 m distance.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Inverse Square Law: For a point source, sound intensity \(I \propto \dfrac{1}{r^2}\).
  • Logarithmic Noise Model: The difference in noise levels due to varying distances is:\[L_2 - L_1 = 20\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\right) \]

4. Solution Method:

Apply the attenuation formula directly to map the decay in decibels from 30 m to 60 m.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Apply the attenuation formula:\[L_2 = L_1 + 20\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{r_1}{r_2}\right) = 74 + 20\log_{10}\left(\dfrac{30}{60}\right) \]\[L_2 = 74 + 20\log_{10}(0.5) \]
  2. Execute computation:\[\log_{10}(0.5) \approx -0.30103 \]\[L_2 = 74 + 20(-0.30103) = 74 - 6.02 = 67.98\text{ dB} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 67.98 dB | Accepted key range: 67 to 69

questions.title: GATE CE 2016 Set 2 | CE Q52
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: For a wastewater sample, the three-day biochemical oxygen demand at incubation temperature of 20°C (BOD₃day, 20°C) is estimated as 200 mg/L. Taking the value of the first order BOD reaction rate constant as 0.22 day⁻¹, the five-day BOD (expressed in mg/L) of the wastewater at incubation temperature of 20°C (BOD₅day, 20°C) would be _________
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Engineering

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • 3-day BOD: \(BOD_3 = 200\text{ mg/L}\)
    • Reaction rate constant: \(k = 0.22\text{ day}^{-1}\) at \(20^\circ\text{C}\)
  • Aim: Determine the 5-day BOD (\(BOD_5\)) at \(20^\circ\text{C}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • BOD Kinetics: Biochemical Oxygen Demand follows first-order reaction kinetics.
  • BOD exerted at time \(t\):\[BOD_t = L_0(1 - e^{-kt}) \]where \(L_0\) is the ultimate carbonaceous BOD.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Use known \(BOD_3\) and rate constant to calculate Ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)).
  2. Substitute \(L_0\) into the equation with \(t = 5\text{ days}\) to find \(BOD_5\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Calculate Ultimate BOD (\(L_0\)):\[200 = L_0(1 - e^{-0.22 \times 3}) = L_0(1 - e^{-0.66}) \]\[200 = L_0(1 - 0.51685) = L_0(0.48315) \]\[L_0 = \dfrac{200}{0.48315} = 413.95\text{ mg/L} \]
  2. Calculate 5-day BOD (\(BOD_5\)):\[BOD_5 = 413.95 \times (1 - e^{-0.22 \times 5}) = 413.95 \times (1 - e^{-1.1}) \]\[BOD_5 = 413.95 \times (1 - 0.33287) = 413.95 \times 0.66713 = 276.16\text{ mg/L} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 276.16 mg/L | Accepted key range: 275 to 278

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen (TKN) concentration (mg/L as N) in domestic sewage is the sum of the concentrations of:
options: organic and inorganic nitrogen in sewage
organic nitrogen and nitrate in sewage
organic nitrogen and ammonia in sewage

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: organic and inorganic nitrogen in sewage
structuredOptions.html: organic and inorganic nitrogen in sewage

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: organic nitrogen and nitrate in sewage
structuredOptions.html: organic nitrogen and nitrate in sewage

structuredOptions.label: C
structuredOptions.text: organic nitrogen and ammonia in sewage
structuredOptions.html: organic nitrogen and ammonia in sewage

questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Characteristics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen (TKN)
  • Aim: Identify the individual nitrogen fractions that sum to TKN.

3. Core Concepts:

Nitrogen Forms in Sewage: Nitrogen progressively oxidizes as:
Organic Nitrogen → Ammonia Nitrogen → Nitrite → Nitrate

TKN Definition: Total Kjeldahl Nitrogen evaluates strictly the unoxidized forms. It is the sum of organic nitrogen and ammonia (ammonium) nitrogen. Oxidized forms (nitrites and nitrates) are excluded.

4. Solution Method:

Filter out options incorporating nitrites or nitrates, isolating the fundamental TKN formula.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  • (A) Inorganic nitrogen includes nitrates/nitrites → Incorrect.
  • (B) Contains nitrate → Incorrect.
  • (C) "Organic nitrogen and ammonia" aligns flawlessly with TKN → Correct.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q31
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
Solid waste generated from an industry contains only two components, X and Y as shown in the table below

ComponentComposition (% weight)Density (kg/m³)
Xc₁ρ₁
Yc₂ρ₂

Assuming \((c_1 + c_2) = 100\), the composite density of the solid waste (ρ) is given by:
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Solid Waste Management

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Analysis
  • Given Data:
    • Waste components: X and Y
    • Weight compositions: \(c_1\) and \(c_2\) with \(c_1 + c_2 = 100\)
    • Densities: \(\rho_1\) and \(\rho_2\) (kg/m³)
  • Aim: Formulate the expression for the composite density (\(\rho\)) of the mixed solid waste.

3. Core Concepts:

Composite Density Formula: Mass and volume are additive: \[\rho = \frac{M_{total}}{V_{total}} \]

4. Solution Method:

Use a basis of 100 kg total sample. Determine the volume of each component by dividing its mass by its density. Express composite density as \(M/V\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Basis: \(M_{total} = 100\text{ kg}\)
    Mass of X: \(M_1 = c_1\text{ kg}\), Mass of Y: \(M_2 = c_2\text{ kg}\)
  2. Convert mass to volume:
    \[V_1 = \frac{c_1}{\rho_1}, \quad V_2 = \frac{c_2}{\rho_2}, \quad V_{total} = \frac{c_1}{\rho_1} + \frac{c_2}{\rho_2} \]
  3. Composite density:
    \[\rho = \frac{M_{total}}{V_{total}} = \frac{100}{\left(\dfrac{c_1}{\rho_1} + \dfrac{c_2}{\rho_2}\right)} = 100\left(\frac{c_1}{\rho_1} + \frac{c_2}{\rho_2}\right)^{-1} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: \(\displaystyle 100\left(\frac{c_1}{\rho_1} + \frac{c_2}{\rho_2}\right)^{-1}\)  |  Correct option: (A)

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
The concentration of Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂) in ambient atmosphere was measured as 30 \(\mu\)g/m³. Under the same conditions, the above SO₂ concentration expressed in ppm is __________.

Given: \(P/(RT) = 41.6 \text{ mol/m}^3\); where, P = Pressure; T = Temperature; R = universal gas constant; Molecular weight of SO₂ = 64.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Air Pollution

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Concentration of \(SO_2 = 30\,\mu\text{g/m}^3\)
    • \(P/(RT) = 41.6\text{ mol/m}^3\)
    • Molecular weight of \(SO_2 = 64\text{ g/mol}\)
  • Aim: Express the concentration in parts per million (ppm) by volume.

3. Core Concepts:

By the Ideal Gas Law (\(PV = nRT\)), \(P/(RT)\) represents the total molar density of air (\(n/V\)). The concentration of a gaseous pollutant in ppmv is its mole fraction multiplied by \(10^6\): \[\text{ppm} = \left(\frac{\text{Moles of Pollutant}}{\text{Total Moles of Air}}\right) \times 10^6 \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Find the mass of \(SO_2\) in \(1\text{ m}^3\) of air.
  2. Convert that mass into moles of \(SO_2\).
  3. Divide by the total moles of air in \(1\text{ m}^3\) (given by \(P/RT\)).
  4. Multiply by \(10^6\) to get ppm.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Mass of \(SO_2\) in \(1\text{ m}^3\):
    \[m = 30\,\mu\text{g} = 30 \times 10^{-6}\text{ g} \]
  2. Moles of \(SO_2\) in \(1\text{ m}^3\):
    \[n_{SO_2} = \frac{30 \times 10^{-6}}{64} = 4.6875 \times 10^{-7}\text{ mol} \]
  3. Total moles of air per m³:
    \[n_{\text{air}} = \frac{P}{RT} = 41.6\text{ mol} \]
  4. Calculate ppm:
    \[\text{ppm} = \frac{4.6875 \times 10^{-7}}{41.6} \times 10^6 = 1.1268 \times 10^{-8} \times 10^6 = 0.011268 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.011 ppm  |  Accepted key range: 0.010 to 0.012

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 1 | CE Q60
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question:
Consider a primary sedimentation tank (PST) in a water treatment plant with Surface Overflow Rate (SOR) of 40 m³/m²/d. The diameter of the spherical particle which will have 90 percent theoretical removal efficiency in this tank is __________ \(\mu\)m. Assume that settling velocity of the particles in water is described by Stokes’s Law.

Given: Density of water = 1000 kg/m³; Density of particle = 2650 kg/m³; g = 9.81 m/s²; Kinematic viscosity of water (v) = \(1.10 \times 10^{-6}\) m²/s
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment (Sedimentation)

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Surface Overflow Rate (SOR): \(v_o = 40\text{ m}^3/\text{m}^2/\text{d}\)
    • Theoretical removal efficiency: \(\eta = 90\%\)
    • Density of water: \(\rho_w = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\)
    • Density of particle: \(\rho_p = 2650\text{ kg/m}^3\)
    • Kinematic viscosity: \(\nu = 1.10 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}^2/\text{s}\)
    • Gravity: \(g = 9.81\text{ m/s}^2\)
  • Aim: Calculate the diameter of the spherical particle (\(d\)) in \(\mu\text{m}\).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Removal Efficiency: \(\eta = \dfrac{v_s}{v_o}\), where \(v_s\) is the settling velocity and \(v_o\) is the SOR.
  • Stokes's Law: \[v_s = \frac{g(\rho_p - \rho_w)d^2}{18\mu} = \frac{g\left(\dfrac{\rho_p}{\rho_w}-1\right)d^2}{18\nu} \]

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert SOR (\(v_o\)) to m/s.
  2. Calculate required settling velocity (\(v_s\)) using efficiency.
  3. Apply Stokes's law and solve for \(d\).
  4. Convert \(d\) from meters to \(\mu\text{m}\).

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

  1. Convert \(v_o\):
    \[v_o = \frac{40}{24 \times 3600} = 4.6296 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m/s} \]
  2. Calculate Settling Velocity (\(v_s\)):
    \[v_s = 0.90 \times 4.6296 \times 10^{-4} = 4.1667 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m/s} \]
  3. Apply Stokes's Law to find \(d^2\):
    \[4.1667 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{9.81 \times (2.65 - 1) \times d^2}{18 \times 1.10 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{9.81 \times 1.65 \times d^2}{19.8 \times 10^{-6}} \]\[4.1667 \times 10^{-4} = 817500 \cdot d^2 \]\[d^2 = \frac{4.1667 \times 10^{-4}}{817500} = 5.0968 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}^2 \]
  4. Solve for \(d\):
    \[d = \sqrt{5.0968 \times 10^{-10}} = 2.2576 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 22.576\,\mu\text{m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 22.58 μm  |  Accepted key range: 20.0 to 24.0

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q30
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A groundwater sample was found to contain 500 mg/L total dissolved solids (TDS). TDS (in %) present in the sample is _____________.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Quality Parameters

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) \(= 500\) mg/L
  • Aim: Express the TDS concentration as a percentage (%).

3. Core Concepts:

Percentage Concentration: Calculated as the mass of the solute (TDS) divided by the total mass of the solution (water), multiplied by 100.

Density Assumption: For dilute aqueous solutions (like typical groundwater), the density of the sample is assumed to be identical to pure water: \(\rho \approx 1000\) kg/m³ or \(1\) kg/L.

4. Solution Method:

  1. Convert the volume of 1 Liter of water to its equivalent mass in milligrams (mg) to establish a standard mass-to-mass ratio.
  2. Divide the mass of TDS by the mass of 1 Liter of water and multiply by 100 to get the percentage.

5. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Determine the mass of 1 L of water\[1 \text{ Liter of water} = 1 \text{ kg} = 1000 \text{ g} = 1{,}000{,}000 \text{ mg} = 10^6 \text{ mg} \]

Step 2: Compute percentage\[\text{TDS (in \%)} = \left(\frac{\text{Mass of TDS}}{\text{Total Mass of Water}}\right) \times 100 \]\[\text{TDS (in \%)} = \left(\frac{500}{1{,}000{,}000}\right) \times 100 = 0.0005 \times 100 = 0.05\% \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 0.05%  |  Accepted key range: 0.05 to 0.05

questions.explanation:

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Recall
  • Given Data: Pollutants: Sulfur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)) and Carbon monoxide (\(\text{CO}\)).
  • Aim: Identify the primary adverse physiological effects of these specific gases on humans.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Sulfur Dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)): A highly reactive gas that is a severe respiratory irritant. Upon inhalation, it causes inflammation of the respiratory tract, severely affecting the lungs and aggravating asthma and bronchitis.

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q57
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A landfill is to be designed to serve a population of 200000 for a period of 25 years. The solid waste (SW) generation is 2 kg/person/day. The density of the un-compacted SW is 100 kg/m³ and a compaction ratio of 4 is suggested. The ratio of compacted fill (i.e., SW + cover) to compacted SW is 1.5. The landfill volume (in million m³) required is _____________.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Solid Waste Management

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Population \(= 200{,}000\)
    • Design life \(= 25\) years
    • SW generation rate \(= 2\) kg/person/day
    • Un-compacted SW density \(= 100\) kg/m³
    • Compaction ratio \(= 4\)
    • Compacted fill (SW + cover) to compacted SW ratio \(= 1.5\)
  • Aim: Calculate required total landfill volume.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Mass of Solid Waste: \(M = \text{Population} \times \text{Rate} \times \text{Time}\)
  • Compaction Ratio: \(CR = \dfrac{V_{\text{uncompacted}}}{V_{\text{compacted}}}\)
  • Cover Material Allowance: Multiplier to find total volume including daily soil covers.

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Total Mass Generation\[M = 200{,}000 \times 2 \times (25 \times 365) = 3.65 \times 10^9 \text{ kg} \]

Step 2: Volume of Un-compacted SW\[V_{\text{uncompacted}} = \frac{3.65 \times 10^9}{100} = 36.5 \times 10^6 \text{ m}^3 \]

Step 3: Compacted SW Volume\[V_{\text{compacted SW}} = \frac{36.5 \times 10^6}{4} = 9.125 \times 10^6 \text{ m}^3 \]

Step 4: Total Landfill Volume\[V_{\text{landfill}} = 1.5 \times 9.125 \times 10^6 = 13.6875 \times 10^6 \text{ m}^3 \]Note: If leap years are considered (365.25 days/year), volume \(= 13.69\) million m³, falling safely within the same key range.

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 13.68 million m³  |  Accepted key range: 13.6 to 13.8

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q58
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: A water treatment plant of capacity, 1 m³/s has filter boxes of dimensions 6 m × 10 m. Loading rate to the filters is 120 m³/day/m². When two of the filters are out of service for back washing, the loading rate (in m³/day/m²) is _____________.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Water Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Plant Capacity: \(Q = 1\) m³/s \(= 86{,}400\) m³/day
    • Filter box dimensions: \(6\) m \(\times\) \(10\) m \(= 60\) m² per filter
    • Design loading rate: \(120\) m³/day/m²
    • Number of filters out of service: \(2\)
  • Aim: Evaluate new loading rate on remaining operational filters.

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total design area required: \(A_{\text{total}} = \dfrac{Q}{\text{Design Loading Rate}}\)
  • Total number of filter units: \(N = \dfrac{A_{\text{total}}}{A_{\text{individual}}}\)
  • New Loading Rate: \(LR_{\text{new}} = \dfrac{Q}{(N-2) \times A_{\text{individual}}}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Total initial filter area and number of filters\[A_{\text{total}} = \frac{86{,}400}{120} = 720 \text{ m}^2 \]\[N = \frac{720}{60} = 12 \text{ filters} \]

Step 2: New effective area after backwashing isolation
Operational filters \(= 12 - 2 = 10\)\[A_{\text{active}} = 10 \times 60 = 600 \text{ m}^2 \]

Step 3: Calculate new loading rate\[LR_{\text{new}} = \frac{86{,}400}{600} = 144 \text{ m}^3/\text{day/m}^2 \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 144 m³/day/m²  |  Accepted key range: 144

questions.title: GATE CE 2015 Set 2 | CE Q59
questions.subject: Environmental Engineering
questions.question: Ultimate BOD of a river water sample is 20 mg/L. BOD rate constant (natural log) is 0.15 day⁻¹. The respective values of BOD (in %) exerted and remaining after 7 days are:
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Characteristics

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Application
  • Given Data:
    • Ultimate BOD: \(L_0 = 20\) mg/L
    • BOD rate constant (base \(e\)): \(k = 0.15\) day\(^{-1}\)
    • Time: \(t = 7\) days
  • Aim: Percentage of BOD exerted and remaining after 7 days.

3. Core Concepts:

First-order BOD kinetic equations:

  • BOD Exerted: \(Y_t = L_0(1 - e^{-kt})\)
  • BOD Remaining: \(L_t = L_0\, e^{-kt}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Calculate Remaining Fraction\[e^{-kt} = e^{-0.15 \times 7} = e^{-1.05} \approx 0.3499 \]BOD remaining \(\approx\) 35%

Step 2: Calculate Exerted Fraction\[1 - 0.3499 = 0.6501 \]BOD exerted \(\approx\) 65%

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 65% exerted and 35% remaining  |  Correct option: (C)

questions.question: In a wastewater treatment plant, primary sedimentation tank (PST) designed at an overflow rate of 32.5 m³/day/m² is 32.5 m long, 8.0 m wide and liquid depth of 2.25 m. If the length of the weir is 75 m, the weir loading rate (in m³/day/m) is _____________.
questions.explanation:
Environmental Engineering | Wastewater Treatment

2. Problem Analysis:

  • Taxonomy: Comprehension
  • Given Data:
    • Overflow rate: \(V_o = 32.5\) m³/day/m²
    • PST dimensions: Length \(= 32.5\) m, Width \(= 8.0\) m, Depth \(= 2.25\) m
    • Weir length: \(L_w = 75\) m
  • Aim: Calculate the Weir Loading Rate (WLR).

3. Core Concepts:

  • Total Discharge: \(Q = \text{Overflow Rate} \times \text{Surface Area}\)
    Note: Depth data is purely distractor information and is not needed here.
  • Weir Loading Rate: \(WLR = \dfrac{Q}{L_w}\)

4. Step-by-Step Execution:

Step 1: Determine Total Discharge Volume\[A = 32.5 \times 8.0 = 260 \text{ m}^2 \]\[Q = 32.5 \times 260 = 8{,}450 \text{ m}^3/\text{day} \]

Step 2: Evaluate Weir Loading Rate\[WLR = \frac{8{,}450}{75} = 112.67 \text{ m}^3/\text{day/m} \]

6. Final Answer:

Final Answer: 112.67 m³/day/m  |  Accepted key range: 112.0 to 113.0
